verses: Not for the stormy wind, Nor rushing chariots' roar, But when I view the road to Chou,— I'm pained to my heart's core.
Not for the whirlwind's sweep, Nor car's unsteady roll, But when I view the road to Chou,— Deep sadness dulls my soul.
For one who fish can cook, His boilers I would clear; So him whose heart beats westward true, With these good words I cheer.
